heading: Privacy and data-protection baseline
paragraph: The Privacy Ceiling is derived from the strongest compatible protection required across the supported United States jurisdictions, the United Kingdom and the European Union/EEA, plus deliberate engineering headroom. The implementation MUST maintain a versioned LegalPrivacyProfile describing the currently applicable statutory/regulatory requirements for each supported jurisdiction. Where multiple requirements are compatible, the most protective requirement becomes the global default. Where applicable laws genuinely conflict, the exception MUST be narrowly jurisdiction-scoped, documented, legally reviewed and MUST NOT lower protection for unaffected users or data.
criterion: The Privacy Ceiling is derived from the strongest compatible protection required across the supported United States jurisdictions, the United Kingdom and the European Union/EEA, plus deliberate engineering headroom.

heading: Risk classification and sensitive actions
paragraph: For every elevated request, Home MUST show an impact preview containing all determinable affected object types, counts and scopes before execution. heading: First-party Sites URL namespace
paragraph: The site slug and Sites-managed route segments use the restricted lowercase character set a-z and hyphen; slash is the path-segment separator. A segment MUST NOT begin or end with a hyphen, and empty/repeated path segments are rejected. Sites normalises valid input to one canonical URL representation rather than allowing visually ambiguous aliases.

heading: TF-02 — Shared UI, navigation and authoring behaviour
paragraph: Inline and pop-up editors MUST visibly identify the source document and whether edits affect the original. Pop-ups require a title, Close, Open in owning app and permission/save state, plus Back or breadcrumbs when navigating within a nested container. Closing returns focus and the surrounding view to the originating item. Escape closes the innermost dismissible surface, not an unrelated outer editor; modal surfaces use the shared focus/inert contract. Dismissal MUST NOT discard uncommitted edits. Where a full-screen mobile view replaces a desktop pop-up, Back returns to the same contextual location.
criterion: Inline and pop-up editors MUST visibly identify the source document and whether edits affect the original.

heading: TF-02 — Shared UI, navigation and authoring behaviour
paragraph: Inline and pop-up editors MUST visibly identify the source document and whether edits affect the original. Pop-ups require a title, Close, Open in owning app and permission/save state, plus Back or breadcrumbs when navigating within a nested container. Closing returns focus and the surrounding view to the originating item. Escape closes the innermost dismissible surface, not an unrelated outer editor; modal surfaces use the shared focus/inert contract. Dismissal MUST NOT discard uncommitted edits. Where a full-screen mobile view replaces a desktop pop-up, Back returns to the same contextual location.
criterion: Where a full-screen mobile view replaces a desktop pop-up, Back returns to the same contextual location.

heading: TF-03 — Common data, source references and recovery
paragraph: A source reference MUST identify the canonical file/artifact, owning app, optional stable sub-object/section selector and revision policy. Ordinary references follow the current authorised source by default; an explicitly pinned revision and every Replay checkpoint identify a specific historical revision. Repeated appearances MAY have different local layout or labels while referring to the same original. Renaming or moving a source MUST NOT detach references. Deleting a selected source section produces a visible missing-section state; the app MUST NOT silently substitute the whole document or a different section.

paragraph: Access to a container or composed document MUST NOT grant access to its sources. heading: TF-03 — Common data, source references and recovery
paragraph: Removing an appearance, connection or authored block removes that contextual object only. Deleting an original invokes the owning Files/app operation and its confirmation, Trash and recovery rules. Duplicating a placement or composed document preserves references by default; duplicating source content requires a separately labelled Make independent copy action, appropriate rights and an explicit destination. The UI MUST preview the difference before a consequential operation. Undo/redo MUST act on the same semantic operation and respect current revisions; it MUST NOT reverse unrelated collaborators' changes.

heading: TF-03 — Common data, source references and recovery
paragraph: Mutations MUST be validated and committed atomically at the smallest user-visible boundary using stable operation identity and expected/base revisions. Real-time updates and offline journals inherit the existing Files and owning-app contracts. Concurrent incompatible edits produce recoverable conflicts, not silent last-write-wins. Invalid edits preserve the last valid state and the recoverable draft. Save failure MUST remain visible until durability is established. Content and referenced assets MUST not be evicted while they are the only unsynced copy.

paragraph: Every non-Folder type is a first-class versioned Files organisation object with a stable Files item identity, type, storage location, settings and local membership/layout records. heading: TF-P01 — Product boundary and editor layout
paragraph: The editor MUST provide a component/object library, an object hierarchy, a central Design surface, a Logic/relationships surface, a contextual property inspector and a Run/Preview surface. heading: TF-P02 — Typed model, logic and execution
paragraph: Run/Preview shows the interactive output with Play/Run, Pause/Stop where time-based execution applies, Reset and inspectable current input/output values. Runtime experimentation MUST be separate from saved authoring defaults: moving a slider during a viewer session changes that session, not every reader's shared model. An editor can explicitly apply chosen inputs as new defaults. Reset restores the declared initial state; reopening an authored model MUST not silently resume unintended external actions. Controlled calculations with the same revision and inputs MUST behave consistently; nondeterministic inputs and random seeds MUST be declared when used.

heading: TF-H02 — Reader experience and durable progress

heading: TF-H02 — Reader experience and durable progress

Opening an embedded file or Prototype obeys its own permissions, and completion MUST depend on an explicit typed result, not a fragile guess from visible pixels.

paragraph: Capture records MUST include SessionID, authorised source identities, ordered EventIDs, event/revision provenance, CheckpointIDs, timestamps/sequence, required base revisions or validated snapshot references, annotations and media references. heading: TF-R03 — Review, sharing, failure and acceptance
paragraph: Before sharing/export, Replay MUST provide an included-material review showing files, revisions, annotations, optional recordings and recipient access implications. Referenced live access and an exported independent snapshot are distinct. Copy/export rights are required for retained source bytes shared independently. Excluding or redacting captured content MUST also address derived thumbnails, search text, transcripts and dependent snapshots; metadata MUST not leak a supposedly removed secret. A presentation trim alone MUST not be labelled permanent redaction.

heading: TF-X02 — Canonical API action catalogue
paragraph: Every mutation request MUST include the target stable IDs, typed payload, operation/idempotency key and expected revision, or an explicitly declared create precondition. Successful results identify affected objects, resulting revision and any job/change-event identity. Long-running query, capture, evaluation, export and merge work exposes JobID, progress, cancellation and durable result/error. Events have stable IDs and resumable cursors. Home resolves caller identity, scopes and risk before dispatch; possession of an ID never grants access.

heading: TF-X03 — Platforms, responsive behaviour and resource limits
paragraph: Large collections/graphs/documents MUST use bounded incremental loading, preview hydration, virtualisation and subscription cleanup. Closed/off-screen embeds MUST not continue uncontrolled computation, media playback or capture. Source resolution and exports MUST detect recursion and bound dependency traversal. Query, evaluation, capture, import/export and merge limits MUST be declared by the relevant capability and shown before an operation that exceeds them; limits MUST not silently truncate content. Existing platform-wide performance/resource thresholds remain mandatory. Actual supported workload sizes and measured results MUST be recorded rather than invented completion claims.
